title: Minimum Paper Tables for Skeptical Reviewer
rationale: Five tables that cover method, validation, decomposition, normalization, and mechanism. A skeptical magnetospheric physicist needs: (1) proof it works on their data, (2) proof it adds value beyond their tools, (3) proof the math isn't hiding artifacts, (4) proof the physics is interpretable.

table_1_baseline_comparison.purpose: Shows the CD associator adds value beyond standard diagnostics
table_1_baseline_comparison.data_source: THEMIS-A Oct 2008, 118 curated Zenodo V2 crossings
table_1_baseline_comparison.key_finding: CD matches PVI sensitivity with half the false alarms. Kurtosis (28%) proves CD is not a high-order moment proxy.

table_2_curated_validation.note: Only curated/algorithmic labels. No heuristic rows.
table_2_curated_validation.key_finding: 89% detection against expert magnetopause labels. Curated labels consistently double detection rates vs heuristics.

table_3_normalization_ladder.purpose: Proves the cavity result is not purely normalization artifact
table_3_normalization_ladder.key_finding: Direction-only preserves 1.9x genuine cavity contrast. Raw reverses entirely. ZD audit confirms: not an algebraic artifact (ratio 0.963).

table_4_decomposition_summary.purpose: Shows the observable is physically interpretable, not a black box
rows: Real < shared < indep: phase coupling suppresses
Compressive modes elevate at dipolar boundaries
table_4_decomposition_summary.key_finding: The CD associator measures effective dimensionality of organized phase coupling. Coherent structures collapse to few dimensions (low A); turbulent boundaries expand to many (high A).

table_5_dimension_sweep.purpose: Justifies the choice of 32D and shows the detection-selectivity trade-off
table_5_dimension_sweep.key_finding: 16D is most sensitive, 32D is most selective. No topological phase transition -- smooth trade-off. 32D balances detection and selectivity.
